newsitem.title: UK: Five hurt in Guinness helicopter crash-landing.
newsitem.headline: Five hurt in Guinness helicopter crash-landing.

text.p: Five people were injured when a helicopter taking part in a promotional trip for brewing firm Guinness Ireland crash-landed near Enniskillen in Northern Ireland on Monday, police said.
A company spokesman said in Dubllin the managing director of Guinness Northern Ireland, Brian Duffy, was believed to be one of the passengers. He seemed shaken but not seriously hurt.

"At the moment we have three casualties who have arrived. We are expecting two others," a hospital source in Enniskillen told Reuters. Two of the casualties were in a stable condition and the third "is considered ill at the moment," the source said.
The helicopter was believed to be carrying five people -- the pilot, the Guinness executive and three journalists.
It was one of three aircraft taking part in the launch of a marketing campaign for Guinness, the company spokesman said.
"It would appear that a bird flew into the rear rotor of the helicopter, and the helicopter came down."

First reports indicated that one of the journalists, Jim McDowell, northern editor of the Sunday World newspaper, was being treated in hospital while Barbara McCann, GMTV reporter in Belfast, was being treated by "medical people on the ground".
The spokesman said the reports suggested that that Duffy, Joe Kearney of the Irish News in Belfast, and the pilot, whose name was not known, "seemed to be shaken but seemed to be okay".
